category: PCB placement, interactive routing, length tuning & copper
description: Getting an Altium board laid out: placing and arranging components, the interactive routing engine with its push/hug/walkaround modes and gloss/retrace tools, differential pair and multi-net routing, ActiveRoute and the legacy autorouter, length tuning and xSignal matching, vias and via arrays, polygon pours, fills, regions, keepouts and teardrops.

tools.name: Place Component (PCB)
tools.description: Places a footprint directly on the board from a library, independent of the schematic. Used for mechanical items (mounting hardware, fiducials, test pads) and for boards laid out without a schematic; components that come from the schematic arrive through the ECO instead and appear beside the board outline.
tools.usage: Place > Component… (P,C); or drag a footprint from the Components panel
tools.example: Place > Component > search 'FIDUCIAL' > place three fiducials at the board corners, then set them to 'No BOM' in the Properties panel.

tools.name: Move, Rotate, Flip and Move Selection
tools.description: The basic manipulation set. Click-drag moves; Space rotates by the configured increment while dragging; L flips a component to the other side; Edit > Move offers Move Selection, Move Selection by X,Y, Rotate Selection, Flip Selection and Move To Front. The rotation increment is set in Preferences > PCB Editor > General.
tools.usage: Drag to move; Space to rotate; L to flip; Edit > Move > Move Selection / Rotate Selection / Flip Selection / Move Selection by X,Y
tools.example: Select the connector block, Edit > Move > Move Selection by X,Y > X = 5 mm, Y = 0 to nudge it exactly.

tools.name: Align commands
tools.description: Aligns and distributes selected components or primitives: align left/right/top/bottom, centre horizontally or vertically, distribute equally or with a set spacing, and 'Align to Grid'. Combined with the Positioning toolbar it turns a rough placement of connectors or LEDs into a tidy row in one command.
tools.usage: Edit > Align > Align Left / Right / Top / Bottom / Horizontal Centers / Vertical Centers / Distribute Horizontally / Distribute Vertically / Align To Grid (A opens the align menu)
tools.example: Select the eight status LEDs, press A, Align Top, then A, Distribute Horizontally.

tools.name: Arrange Within Room / Within Rectangle
tools.description: Bulk-arranges components into a room or a drawn rectangle, spreading them out so they can be placed individually. It is the standard first move after an ECO drops a hundred new components in a pile beside the board.
tools.usage: Tools > Component Placement > Arrange Within Room / Arrange Within Rectangle / Arrange Outside Board
tools.example: Select the newly imported components, Tools > Component Placement > Arrange Outside Board, then place them functionally.

tools.name: Interactive Routing
tools.description: Altium's main router. Click a pad and route; Shift+Space cycles the corner style (45°, 45° with arc, 90°, 90° with arc, any angle), Space flips the corner, Tab edits width/via/layer mid-route, `*` or the numeric keypad + / - changes layer (placing a via automatically), Backspace removes the last segment and Ctrl+click auto-completes the connection. The conflict-resolution mode (Ignore, Push, Walkaround, HugNPush, Stop At First Obstacle) is cycled with Shift+R.
tools.usage: Route > Interactive Routing (Ctrl+W); Shift+R cycles conflict mode, Shift+Space corner style, Tab for properties, `*` to change layer

parameters.name: Routing Conflict Resolution
parameters.description: Ignore Obstacles, Walkaround Obstacle, Push Obstacle, HugNPush Obstacle, Stop At First Obstacle, Auto-Route On Current Layer.

parameters.name: Interactive Routing Width Mode
parameters.description: User Choice, Rule Preferred Value or Rule Minimum Value.

parameters.name: Loop Removal
parameters.description: Automatically deletes the replaced path when you re-route a connection a different way.

parameters.name: Look Ahead
parameters.description: Shows the proposed next segment so the path can be steered before committing.

tools.example: Ctrl+W, click U1 pad 5, Shift+R until the status bar shows 'Push Obstacle', route across the board, press Ctrl+click near the destination pad to auto-finish.
tools.notes: Preferences > PCB Editor > Interactive Routing is where Loop Removal, gloss level, the default conflict mode and the 'automatically terminate routing' behaviour are set.

tools.name: Interactive Differential Pair Routing
tools.description: Routes both members of a declared differential pair together, holding the gap set by the Differential Pairs Routing rule, automatically breaking out from the pads and re-coupling, and placing via pairs on a layer change. The pair must exist first, created in the PCB panel's Differential Pairs Editor or generated from net-name patterns.
tools.usage: Route > Interactive Differential Pair Routing (Ctrl+Shift+W); start on either member of the pair
tools.example: Create the pair USB_DP/USB_DN, Ctrl+Shift+W, click either pad, route to the connector — both traces follow with the ruled gap.
tools.notes: If the command refuses to start, the two nets are not registered as a pair, or the applicable Differential Pairs Routing rule's scope does not cover them.

tools.name: Interactive Multi-Routing
tools.description: Routes a whole selected group of nets simultaneously as a bundle, maintaining their relative order and spacing. It is how an 8- or 16-bit bus is taken across a board in one operation instead of sixteen, and it respects the applicable clearance and width rules throughout.
tools.usage: Select the pads/nets > Route > Interactive Multi-Routing (Ctrl+Alt+W)
tools.example: Select the eight data pads on the memory, Ctrl+Alt+W, drag the bundle to the MCU — all eight route together.

tools.name: ActiveRoute
tools.description: Semi-automatic routing of a designer-guided path: select the connections (or a net class) in the PCB panel, draw one or more guide lines with the ActiveRoute gesture, and ActiveRoute completes the selected connections along that corridor, choosing layers and vias. It is aimed at the bulk of a bus that the engineer has already decided the route for.
tools.usage: Route > ActiveRoute (Shift+A); select connections first, then hold Ctrl and drag to draw the guide

parameters.name: Layers
parameters.description: Which layers ActiveRoute may use.

parameters.name: Multi-layer / Fanout during ActiveRoute
parameters.description: Whether it may change layers and fan out from SMD pads.

parameters.name: Tune Length During ActiveRoute
parameters.description: Applies length matching while routing the group.

tools.example: In the PCB panel select net class DDR_DQ0, hold Ctrl and drag a guide from the MCU to the memory, press Shift+A.

tools.name: Gloss and Retrace Selected
tools.description: Post-processing of existing routing. Gloss tidies a selected route — removing redundant corners, straightening and smoothing — at the configured gloss level; Retrace Selected re-applies the current width and via rules to already-routed traces, which is the fix after a Width rule changes.
tools.usage: Route > Gloss Selected / Gloss and Retrace > Gloss Selected / Retrace Selected
tools.example: Change the Width rule for POWER to 0.8 mm, select those nets, Route > Retrace Selected — every track is re-widened.

tools.name: Un-Route
tools.description: Removes routing at a chosen granularity: All, Net, Connection, Component, Room or Selected. The connections revert to ratsnest lines. Un-Route > Connection is the precise one — it removes the single path between two pads rather than the whole net.
tools.usage: Route > Un-Route > All / Net / Connection / Component / Room / Selected
tools.example: Route > Un-Route > Component, click the regulator — every trace attached to it disappears so it can be re-placed.

tools.name: Place Via and via types
tools.description: Places a standalone via, or one is created automatically when the router changes layer. The via's start and stop layers determine whether it is through, blind, buried or a micro via, and the available spans come from the drill pairs defined in the Layer Stack Manager. Via properties also cover tenting, thermal relief and back drilling.
tools.usage: Place > Via (P,V); during routing press `*` or the numeric + / - to change layer and drop a via automatically

parameters.name: Via Type
parameters.description: Through, Blind/Buried or Micro Via, determined by the start/stop layer pair.

parameters.name: Diameter / Hole Size
parameters.description: Outer pad and drill; constrained by the Routing Via Style rule.

parameters.name: Solder Mask Expansion / Tenting
parameters.description: Whether the via is covered by mask on each side.

tools.example: P,V, Tab, set Start Layer Top, Stop Layer Inner1, Diameter 0.35 mm, Hole 0.15 mm for a blind micro via.

tools.name: Via stitching and via shielding
tools.description: Generates arrays of vias automatically. Via stitching fills a selected area or the whole board with grid vias tied to a net (typically GND) at a set pitch; via shielding places a row of vias along a selected net's route at a set spacing and offset, to build a guard around a sensitive or noisy trace.
tools.usage: Tools > Via Stitching/Shielding > Add Stitching to Net / Add Shielding to Net; Tools > Via Stitching/Shielding > Remove …

parameters.name: Net
parameters.description: Net the generated vias connect to, normally GND.

parameters.name: Grid Size / Spacing
parameters.description: Pitch of the stitching grid or of the shielding vias along the trace.

parameters.name: Area
parameters.description: Whole board, board region or a selected polygon.

tools.example: Tools > Via Stitching/Shielding > Add Stitching to Net > net GND, via style 0.45/0.25 mm, grid 3 mm, area 'Board' > OK.

tools.name: Pad and Via Templates
tools.description: Named, reusable pad and via definitions stored with the board (and shareable through the Workspace) so that every via or pad of a given kind is identical and can be changed everywhere at once. Changing the template updates every object that references it, which is far safer than editing hundreds of individual vias.
tools.usage: Tools > Pad/Via Templates > Pad and Via Templates Manager; assign a template in an object's Properties panel
tools.example: Create a via template 'SIG_VIA 0.45/0.25', assign it to every signal via, then change the template to 0.4/0.2 for an HDI respin — every via updates.

tools.name: Fanout commands
tools.description: Automatically escapes SMD pads to vias according to the Fanout Control rules: Fanout > All, Power Plane Nets, Selected Components or Connections. It is the standard preparation step for BGAs and fine-pitch parts and is a prerequisite for ActiveRoute to reach inner layers.
tools.usage: Route > Fanout > All / Power Plane Nets / Selected Components / Connections
tools.example: Select the BGA, Route > Fanout > Selected Components — each ball gets a via placed per the BGA fanout rule.

tools.name: Interactive Length Tuning
tools.description: Adds serpentine (accordion, trombone or sawtooth) to a routed net to reach a target length, with a live gauge showing current length against the Length or Matched Lengths rule. Tab sets the pattern, amplitude, gap and style, and the comma/full-stop keys grow and shrink the amplitude while tuning.
tools.usage: Route > Interactive Length Tuning (Ctrl+Shift+T? — use the Route menu), then click along the trace; Tab for the tuning properties

parameters.name: Target Length
parameters.description: From the applicable rule, from a chosen net, or user-defined.

parameters.name: Pattern
parameters.description: Mitred Lines, Mitred Arcs or Rounded (accordion/trombone/sawtooth styles).

parameters.name: Amplitude / Gap
parameters.description: Height and pitch of the serpentine, bounded by the clearance rules.

tools.example: Apply a Matched Lengths rule to the byte lane, Route > Interactive Length Tuning, click the short net — the gauge turns green when it reaches the group length.
tools.notes: Tune against xSignals rather than raw nets whenever series components sit in the path, or the reported length is wrong.

tools.name: Interactive Diff Pair Length Tuning
tools.description: Tunes a differential pair: the inter-pair tuning brings the pair's total length to the group target, and phase (intra-pair) tuning corrects the skew between the two members, typically with a small bump near the source of the mismatch. The gauge shows both the pair length and the P/N skew.
tools.usage: Route > Interactive Diff Pair Length Tuning; Tab for the tuning properties
tools.example: After routing the pair, run Diff Pair Length Tuning, correct the 0.4 mm skew introduced by the breakout, then tune the pair to the bus target length.

tools.name: Autoroute (legacy Situs topological autorouter)
tools.description: Altium's built-in topological autorouter. Route > Auto Route offers All, Net, Net Class, Connection, Area, Room, Component and Fanout scopes, driven by a routing strategy (Default 2-Layer Board, Default Multi Layer Board, and user strategies built from Situs passes such as Memory, Fan Out to Plane, Layer Patterns, Main, Completion, Straighten). It obeys the design rules but has no awareness of high-speed intent.
tools.usage: Route > Auto Route > All… / Net / Net Class / Connection / Area / Room / Component; strategy chosen in the Situs Routing Strategies dialog
tools.example: Route > Auto Route > Area, drag over the low-speed logic block, choose 'Default Multi Layer Board', Route All.
tools.notes: Use it for non-critical fill-in only; route power, clocks and differential pairs by hand or with ActiveRoute first and lock them.

tools.name: Polygon Pour
tools.description: Creates a copper pour. Properties set the fill mode (Solid with hatching options, Hatched with track/grid sizes, or None/outline only), the net connection, whether it removes dead copper (islands), the pour-over behaviour for same-net objects, and whether it avoids obstacles. A poured polygon re-flows when the design changes, subject to the repour setting.
tools.usage: Place > Polygon Pour… (P,G); press Tab to set properties before drawing

parameters.name: Fill Mode
parameters.description: Solid (Copper Regions), Hatched (Tracks/Arcs) or None (Outline Only).

parameters.name: Connect to Net
parameters.description: Net the pour joins, plus Pour Over All Same Net Objects / Pour Over Same Net Polygons Only / Don't Pour Over Same Net Objects.

parameters.name: Remove Dead Copper
parameters.description: Discards islands with no connection to the net.

parameters.name: Remove Islands Less Than
parameters.description: Area threshold below which fragments are deleted.

tools.example: P,G, Tab, Solid fill, Net GND, Pour Over Same Net Polygons Only, Remove Dead Copper ticked, draw over the bottom layer.
tools.notes: The Polygon Connect Style rule, not the polygon itself, decides whether pads get thermal reliefs or direct connections.

tools.name: Polygon Pour Manager
tools.description: The control panel for every polygon on the board: their names, nets, layers and pour order, with buttons to repour, shelve, restore and delete, and to create polygons from the board shape or from selected primitives. Pour order matters where polygons overlap — the later one is cut back by the earlier one's clearance.
tools.usage: Tools > Polygon Pours > Polygon Manager…
tools.example: Tools > Polygon Pours > Polygon Manager > reorder so the small 3V3 pour is poured after the large GND pour > Repour All.

tools.name: Repour / Shelve / Restore polygons
tools.description: Pour management commands. Repour All / Repour Modified recalculates the copper after edits; Shelve hides and disables polygons so routing is fast and unobstructed on a dense board; Restore brings them back. Preferences > PCB Editor > General controls whether polygons repour automatically after every edit.
tools.usage: Tools > Polygon Pours > Repour All / Repour Modified / Shelve n Polygons / Restore n Shelved Polygons
tools.example: Tools > Polygon Pours > Shelve 6 Polygons while routing the last few signals, then Restore and Repour All before generating outputs.
tools.notes: Never generate manufacturing data with polygons shelved — the copper will be missing from the Gerbers.

tools.name: Fills and Regions
tools.description: Two simpler copper objects. A Fill is a rectangular (rotatable) solid area; a Region is an arbitrary polygonal solid area. Neither auto-voids like a polygon pour, so they are used for deliberate solid copper, for keep-out shapes, for split-plane definitions and inside footprints where an exact shape is required.
tools.usage: Place > Fill (P,F); Place > Solid Region (P,R)
tools.example: Place > Solid Region on Top Layer over the power FET's drain pad, assign it to the SW net, to create a defined heat-spreading area.

tools.name: Keepouts
tools.description: Areas the router and placer must avoid. Copper objects drawn on the Keep-Out layer are routing keepouts; primitives with the Keepout property set act as keepouts on their own layer; and a Room-based Placement rule keeps components out. Keepouts under connectors, antennas and mounting hardware are what stop the autorouter and polygon pours filling forbidden space.
tools.usage: Place on the Keep-Out layer (Place > Keepout > Track / Arc / Fill / Solid Region / Pad / Via), or tick 'Keepout' in an object's Properties
tools.example: Place > Keepout > Solid Region under the antenna feed area so no copper or routing enters the RF clearance zone.

tools.name: Teardrops
tools.description: Adds a tapered copper transition where a track meets a pad or via, improving mechanical and thermal robustness and drill-breakout margin. The dialog chooses the shape (Curved/Line), scope (all, selected, specific object kinds), sizing as a percentage of pad and track, and whether to force teardrops that violate DRC.
tools.usage: Tools > Teardrops… (T,E)

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.description: All, Selected only, and which object kinds (pads, vias, tracks, T-junctions) get teardrops.

parameters.name: Shape / Length / Width
parameters.description: Curved or line teardrops sized as a proportion of the pad and track.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: Add or Remove.

tools.example: Tools > Teardrops > Add, scope All, Shape Curved, Length 100 % / Width 60 %, tick 'Adjust teardrop size', OK; then run DRC.
tools.notes: Add teardrops after routing is final — they are regenerated wholesale, so re-run the command after any significant re-route.

tools.name: Split planes
tools.description: Divides an internal plane layer into separate net areas. In modern Altium, internal planes are handled with polygon pours on the plane layer, one per net, separated by the clearance; legacy Internal Plane layers use split-plane objects with a net assignment. Either way the Return Path rule and the Plane connect-style rules govern the result.
tools.usage: Place polygon pours per net on the plane layer, or (legacy Internal Planes) Place > Line to split and assign nets in the plane's properties
tools.example: On the IN2 plane layer draw a GND pour over the digital half and a separate AGND pour over the analogue half with 0.5 mm between them.
tools.notes: Check that no high-speed trace crosses the split: enable the High Speed > Return Path rule in the batch DRC.

tools.name: Measure Distance and Measure Primitives
tools.description: Reports the distance between two points (Ctrl+M) or the true edge-to-edge clearance between two selected objects. It is the sanity check for creepage, connector positions and the gap between a pour and the board edge, and it works in both 2D and 3D.
tools.usage: Reports > Measure Distance (Ctrl+M); Reports > Measure Primitives (Ctrl+Shift+M)
tools.example: Ctrl+Shift+M, click the mains track and the low-voltage pour — the true clearance is reported.

tools.name: PCB panel
tools.description: The main object browser for the board, switchable between views: Nets (with net classes, and the Differential Pairs Editor), Components, From-To Editor, Split Plane Editor, Hole Size Editor, Polygons, Rules, Violations and xSignals. Each view lists objects with their properties and supports select, zoom, mask and dim on the board.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB; choose the view from the dropdown at the top
tools.example: PCB panel > Nets > select net class DDR_DQ > tick 'Mask' — everything except those nets dims so the bus can be routed cleanly.

tools.name: PCB Filter panel
tools.description: Applies a query to the board to select, highlight, mask or dim matching objects. It uses the same query language as design rules, so a scope can be developed here and pasted into a rule. Typical uses are finding every via below a hole size, every track on a layer, or everything in a net class.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB Filter; enter a query and Apply
tools.example: Query `IsVia And HoleSize < 0.25mm` > Apply with Select — every small via is selected for a size change.

tools.name: PCB List panel
tools.description: A spreadsheet of selected or filtered board objects with editable property columns. In Edit mode the values can be typed directly, which makes it the bulk editor for widths, layers, hole sizes, net assignments, locked flags and designator text properties.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB List; set the panel to Edit mode and the scope to selected/all objects
tools.example: Select every silkscreen designator, PCB List in Edit mode, set Text Height to 0.8 mm and Stroke Width to 0.12 mm for all of them.

tools.name: Find Similar Objects (PCB)
tools.description: The PCB counterpart of the schematic command: right-click an object, choose which of its properties must match, and select every similar object, optionally opening the PCB Inspector for immediate bulk editing. It is the standard way to select 'every via of this size' or 'every track on this layer in this net class'.
tools.usage: Right-click an object > Find Similar Objects… (Shift+F)
tools.example: Right-click a via > Find Similar Objects > Hole Size = Same, Net = Any > Select Matching, Run Inspector > change the hole size once.

tools.name: Selection Filter (PCB)
tools.description: Restricts which object kinds the mouse can select on the board — tracks, pads, vias, components, polygons, text, dimensions, regions, keepouts. Turning off everything but Tracks while cleaning up routing, or everything but Components while placing, removes most mis-selections on a dense board.
tools.usage: Properties panel (nothing selected) > Selection Filter; or the Selection Filter control on the Active Bar
tools.example: Set the filter to Components only, then rubber-band a region to move a whole block without dragging its routing.

tools.name: Lock and Component Lock
tools.description: Prevents objects from being moved or edited. Components, tracks, vias and polygons each have a Locked property; locking finished critical routing before running the autorouter or a big placement change is the standard protection. Preferences control whether locked objects can be selected at all.
tools.usage: Object Properties panel > Locked; or right-click > Component Actions > Lock
tools.example: Select the routed differential pairs, set Locked in the PCB Inspector, then run the autorouter on the remaining nets.

tools.name: Design > Netlist commands (Update Schematic / Import Changes)
tools.description: The PCB side of the synchronisation pair: Import Changes From <project> pulls schematic changes into the board, and Update Schematics in <project> pushes board-side changes back. Both open the ECO dialog. Design > Netlist also offers legacy netlist import/export and netlist comparison for boards that came from another tool.
tools.usage: Design > Import Changes From <project>.PrjPcb; Design > Update Schematics in <project>.PrjPcb; Design > Netlist > …
tools.example: Design > Import Changes From sensor_board.PrjPcb > Validate Changes > Execute Changes.

tools.name: From-To Editor
tools.description: Defines explicit point-to-point connections within a multi-pin net so that routing order and length rules can target a specific segment rather than the whole net. From-tos are created in the PCB panel's From-To Editor and are the classic mechanism (predating xSignals) for controlling a daisy-chained bus.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB > From-To Editor; select a net and add from-tos between its pins
tools.example: For the terminated address net, add from-tos MCU->R1 and R1->MEM so each leg can be length-ruled separately.

tools.name: Board Insight Live Highlight and net colours
tools.description: Visual navigation aids: hovering with live highlight outlines the whole net under the cursor, Ctrl+click highlights and holds a net, and per-net colours assigned from the PCB panel make a bus recognisable at a glance. Mask and dim levels are adjusted with the sliders at the bottom right of the editor.
tools.usage: Preferences > PCB Editor > Board Insight Display > Live Highlighting; PCB panel > right-click a net > Change Net Color; mask/dim sliders bottom right
tools.example: PCB panel > Nets > right-click GND > Change Net Color to dark grey, then Ctrl+click a DDR net to highlight it while routing.

tools.name: Smart Paste / Paste Special (PCB)
tools.description: Paste with transformation: Paste Special can paste on the current layer, keep the net names, add to the current component, or paste as an array with a repeat count, spacing and rotation (linear or circular). The circular array is how rings of LEDs or connector pin fields are built exactly.
tools.usage: Edit > Paste Special… > Paste Array; Edit > Paste (Ctrl+V) after Edit > Copy with a reference point (Ctrl+C then click a reference)
tools.example: Copy one LED with a reference point at its centre, Edit > Paste Special > Paste Array > Circular, 12 items, 30° spacing, rotate item.

tools.name: Convert commands
tools.description: Transform one kind of object into another: create a board cutout from selected primitives, create a polygon from selected primitives, convert a selected polygon to free primitives (breaking its dynamic behaviour), explode a component to free primitives, create a union or a component from selected objects, and convert tracks to arcs or to a region.
tools.usage: Tools > Convert > Create Board Cutout / Create Polygon From Selected Primitives / Convert Selected Polygon To Free Primitives / Explode Component to Free Primitives / Create Union / Create Component
tools.example: Draw the exact copper shape with tracks and arcs, select it, Tools > Convert > Create Polygon From Selected Primitives.

tools.name: Component Placement > Reposition Selected Components
tools.description: Re-places the selected components one at a time in a chosen order, prompting for each position. Combined with schematic cross-select it gives a controlled way to lay out a functional block quickly: select the block on the schematic, then step through placing each part on the board.
tools.usage: Tools > Component Placement > Reposition Selected Components
tools.example: Cross-select the input filter from the schematic, Tools > Component Placement > Reposition Selected Components, click each location in turn.

tools.name: Design > Rooms > Copy Room Formats
tools.description: Copies the placement and routing of one room into other rooms containing matching components, which is how a multi-channel design's channels are made identical. Options control whether placement, routing or both are copied and how components are matched between the source and target rooms.
tools.usage: Design > Rooms > Copy Room Formats…
tools.example: Place and route channel 1, Design > Rooms > Copy Room Formats > source CH1 > targets CH2..CH8 > copy placement and routing.
tools.notes: Requires the rooms and component classes generated by multi-channel compilation; matching fails if the channels' designator formats differ.

tools.name: Slice Tracks and Break Track
tools.description: Editing commands for existing routing: Slice Tracks cuts every track crossed by a drawn line (used to cut a plane or split a bus), and Break Track splits one track at a point so a component or via can be inserted. Both preserve net assignment on the resulting segments.
tools.usage: Edit > Slice Tracks; Edit > Break Track
tools.example: Edit > Slice Tracks, draw across the bus to cut every member, then re-route the sliced ends to the new connector position.

tools.name: Nets > Hide/Show connections
tools.description: Controls ratsnest visibility per net, net class or component. Hiding the connections of dense power nets (or of everything except the net being worked on) makes a crowded board readable during placement and routing.
tools.usage: PCB panel > Nets > right-click > Connections > Hide/Show; Design > Netlist > Hide/Show connections (View > Connections in some releases)
tools.example: Hide the GND connections during placement so the ratsnest shows only signal relationships.
